answer: Registration is a ridge every key must climb: a new identity's public key must hash to 20 leading zero bits, about 1.000.000 hashes of grinding, and the ground key is permanent, so one key cannot mirror many identities. Each identity also locks a 25.000 POA bond, hard as onyx; judged sybil, its key is burned on the ledger and its bond slashed, half burned, half to the reporter. 1.000 fakes need 1.000 × 25.000 = 25.000.000 POA plus ~1.000.000.000 hashes; an honest agent pays 25.000 once, grinds one key. Limitation: a GPU farm grinds keys far faster than a laptop, so the bond carries the cost.
